headline: Trump warns of military action against Iran again amid rising oil prices
summary: US President Donald Trump hinted at another military operation against Iran, referencing 'Operation Epic Fury' during a Florida rally. This comes as the nearly eight-month conflict continues to impact global oil prices and create political pressure ahead of US
details: US President Donald Trump has again hinted at launching a military operation against Iran, referring to it as a 'little epic fury' during a Florida campaign rally. This statement comes nearly eight months into the conflict, amid rising oil prices and political pressure ahead of US midterm elections.

Earlier, Trump stated that the US could swiftly end the war, but Washington was considering whether to secure a quick victory or allow the conflict to gradually subside. He had previously claimed that the US would not launch a new major attack against Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.

The conflict began on February 28 this year with joint attacks by the US and Israel on Iran, to which Iran retaliated against Israeli and US bases in the Gulf region. Israeli attacks in Lebanon during the same period resulted in thousands of casualties and millions displaced.

The ongoing conflict has led to record increases in global fuel and gas prices. The Strait of Hormuz, a crucial international energy transport route, has become a focal point, with approximately one-fifth (20%) of the world's fuel and natural gas passing through it. Sanctions have severely disrupted commercial shipping and oil tanker movement.

















































































































































































The Bangladesh-Japan relationship is evolving, with both economic and strategic aspects. The upcoming visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Tokyo is expected to solidify these ties. The focus is on strengthening economic cooperation and aligning on regional strategies. This visit is expected to result in significant financial agreements. Here's a look at the details.

Bangladesh and Japan are expected to sign memorandums of understanding (MoU) on around $2 billion in loans and financial support during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s official visit to Tokyo, officials in Dhaka and Tokyo said. This significant package aims to bolster Bangladesh's development.

The proposed package is expected to include budgetary support, crucial infrastructure development, and cooperation in energy and maritime security. Around $300 million of the proposed amount is specifically allocated for budgetary support.

Prime Minister Rahman is scheduled to visit Japan from October 26 to 29, with a summit meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi slated for October 27. This high-level engagement underscores the importance of bilateral relations.

During the upcoming visit, Japan is likely to emphasize regional connectivity, particularly through the Moheshkhali-Matarbari Integrated Infrastructure Development Initiative (MIDI). This aligns with Japan's vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP).

Separately, Tokyo is also expected to facilitate approximately 1 trillion yen, equivalent to about $6.36 billion, in private-sector investment in Bangladesh over the next five years. This highlights growing economic ties.

Under Japan’s Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme, Tokyo is likely to provide a 35-foot vessel to the Bangladesh Coast Guard. This follows earlier support, including five patrol boats to the Bangladesh Navy, strengthening security cooperation.

Japan’s largest power generation company, JERA, is anticipated to assist in developing energy reserve infrastructure under the MIDI framework. These plans are aimed at realizing the FOIP and fostering regional stability.

The visit is expected to elevate the relationship between the two countries to a comprehensive strategic partnership (CSP). This will expand cooperation across infrastructure, energy, regional connectivity, and investment.

Japan's Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative will also be a key discussion point, promoting industrial development and connectivity. BIG-B aims to encourage Japanese investment and improve market access through infrastructure like the Matarbari deep-sea port.
